name: SAES (Sliding-Window-Averaged Early Stopping)
definition: A training termination criterion that detects structural saturation of the Gaussian population by monitoring the growth rate of primitives, allowing early stopping without ground-truth volumetric metrics.
summary: SAES is a training termination criterion for 3D Gaussian Splatting that prevents over-training by detecting structural saturation through sliding-window-averaged Gaussian population growth rates.
